composition: Co-PET/PA6 sea-island needle-punched nonwoven precursor with source mass ratio3:7, impregnated with PVA and waterborne polyurethane, then alkali-reduced and washed. Exact final component fractions are not reported.

source_Tmax_definition: Table 4 footnote explicitly defines Tmax as the peak temperature of the maximum thermal mass-loss rate; T1/T2 denote first/second mass-loss processes.
source_residue_definition: Own section 2.6 explicitly reports residue at600°C for MF-WPU and MFP-WPU100/75. Table 3 residues are cone calorimeter results and excluded.
washing_state: Initial finished leather base after prescribed alkaline reduction, water and citric-acid preparatory washes; no durability laundering state assigned
sample_state: MF-WPU; initial finished nonwoven-based synthetic leather
treatment_method: The needle-punched co-PET/PA6 precursor was supplied by Mingxin Menorca (Jiangsu). It was immersed in 6% PVA and padded at 35 rpm/0.6MPa, then dried at 120 °C. Waterborne polyurethane was made by prepolymerization/chain extension using IPDI, PPG, phosphorus-containing Frol-326 polyol, DMPA, BEPG, KH-550, TEA and other listed reagents. The emulsion had 30% solids and NCO/OH molar index 1.45; several reaction dwell times and quantities are only described as suitable/appropriate and remain unknown. Impregnation emulsion contained 1.5% slip agent relative to PWPU plus unspecified thickener/defoamer, with 18–25 s viscosity by the source cup method. PVA-impregnated fabric was wetted with PWPU, padded at 20 rpm/0.1MPa and held at 100 °C for about 1 h. It was repeatedly boiled/squeezed in 1% NaOH at 80 °C for 40 min, rinsed 3–5 times with room-temperature deionized water, washed in 2% citric acid at 60 °C for 0.5 h and dried at 100 °C. Frol-326 fraction was 0% of total polyols; source reference contains conventional WPU, not untreated bare fabric.
limitations: The three named finished nonwoven-based leather states match directly across own Table 2 LOI and Table 4 TG. The source separately characterizes WPU films by FTIR; film-only measurements are not paired. Instrument wording contains parenthetical DSC, but the same section explicitly defines a nitrogen TG program and section 2.6/Figure 10/Table 4 independently identify mass loss and derivative mass-loss-rate measurements. The source also places a heating ramp in the cone method; none of its gas/temperature/residue facts is borrowed into TG. T0/T5/T50 entries are retained raw because their ordering and HTML row spans are not fully verified; no thermal thresholds are inferred or corrected. The explicit Table 4 Tmax definition supports the retained first/second peaks. Only source-explicit 600°C residues are retained; the MFP-WPU100 residue is graph-only and remains unknown. Section 2.3 alternates sea/island removal terminology despite consistent precursor 3:7 and roughly 30% mass reduction; final composition is not reconstructed. Source horizontal-burning minima and Raman ratios differ between prose/table/conclusion and are excluded from the paired metrics. Exact WPU recipe dwell times, final fabric component fractions, FR-900 composition/manufacturer, spray drying details and assay replicate counts remain unreported. Original Figure 10 pixels and PDF bytes were unavailable; this is a bounded published-HTML review. Seven other loading/spray states have no matched exact own TG and remain held; literature comparison LOIs are not own observations. Section 2.6 calls the change from 2.59% to 19.54% a 754.44% increase; that percentage expresses their ratio rather than the relative increase. This derived source claim is not used or substituted for either directly reported residue.
pairing_evidence: Own prepared MF-WPU label appears in process Table 1, measured LOI Table 2 and TG Table 4/section 2.6. The explicit common finished-fabric identity supports pairing; no precursor resin or other spray concentration is substituted.
